It treats the definitional phrases "this is the love of God" as identity rather than illustration, collapsing the dictionary's emotional reading and unifying love with knowing, faith 1 Cor 13, and belief as one obedient act. The common interpretations (A, B, C) treat love as God's self-giving nature (agape) and commandment-keeping as its expression or fruit, but the book's explicit readings of the cited texts carry the central identification more precisely.
